subject: Model fit & evals follow-up — tool calling & structured output (Finlytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finlytics.com>, Maya Singh <maya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit & evals follow-up — tool calling & structured output (Finlytics)

Hi Sanjay / Maya,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — great to meet the Finlytics team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: make the LLM-driven alert enrichment pipeline reliably emit structured JSON actions (tool/function calls) that match your schema and can be ingested without manual fixes.
- Constraints: p95 end-to-end latency target ~300ms for the function call path; schema validation failure tolerance <= 5% on production prompts.
- Data sensitivity: some fields are PII; you mentioned wanting Private deployment options for the production integration.

What Redwood will do (proposal)
1) Run model-fit evals across 2–3 candidate models focused on: JSON schema compliance, function-calling reliability (correct action selection + correct argument structure), and quality regression checks against your prompt set.
2) Provide a small automated harness and hand-eval samples. We'll measure: schema pass rate, hallucination rate (incorrect actions), average tokens, and p95 latency under your expected token lengths.
3) Recommend a default model (and a quantized/cost-optimized variant) and an operational policy (retry behavior, idempotency tokens, fallback model).

Immediate asks for your team
- Share the production prompt set (or a representative subset).
- Share the canonical JSON schema you validate against (if you can) and any existing retries/idempotency expectations.

Proposed timeline
- I can have an initial evaluation plan and pilot runs in 3 business days after we get the prompt set + schema. Full report (incl. recommended model + fallback) within 7 business days.

I'll loop in Rishi and Aditya on the technical plan. If that timeline works, please drop the prompt set and schema (or a link) and I'll get the evals kicked off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: none in this message.
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@finlytics.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit & evals follow-up — tool calling & structured output (Finlytics)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — that plan sounds good. A few clarifications from our side before you start: 

- Attached is a representative schema (finlytics_schema_spec_v2.json) and a short set of production prompts (20 examples) — these are examples, not the full production set.
- Retry behavior: our ingest layer expects idempotent actions; if a tool call fails schema validation we currently drop and surface to a queue. Ideally we want a retry policy that preserves idempotency and minimizes duplicates. Can you confirm how Redwood's function-calling SDK handles retries and idempotency tokens?
- Latency: 300ms p95 is our soft target. If a recommended model needs ~1.5x the latency, we need to see a clear accuracy uplift to justify it.

Also looping in Maya, who will own integration on our side. We're happy to start with the 20-example set and expand if you need broader coverage.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Data Products | Finlytics
sanjay@finlytics.com

Subject: Re: Model fit & evals follow-up — tool calling & structured output (Finlytics)

Rishi / Aditya — looping you in to run the pilot evals. Notes from the Finlytics call:

- They want JSON schema compliance high (target >=95% schema pass on the prompt set) and deterministic function-calling outputs where possible.
- Latency constraint p95 ~300ms; cost is a factor — propose we test: redwood-v2-large (baseline), redwood-v2-medium-quant (cost-optimized), and one open model baseline (open-llama-7b-q4) to show delta.
- Key metrics to include in pilot: schema pass rate, false-action rate (action triggered but semantically wrong), retry-induced duplicates, avg tokens, p50/p95 latency.
- Retry policy: we should evaluate 0, 1, and 2 retry policies with idempotency tokens; capture duplicate-action rate for each.

Deliverables I'm asking for:
1) Initial pilot run results (numbers + short writeup) within 3 business days.
2) A recommended model + fallback and operational policy (retries + idempotency guidance).
3) Small test harness + the 20-example prompt set in the repo we can hand to Finlytics.

Aditya: can you attach the prompt set you want to run and a short README for the eval harness? Rishi: please keep an eye on latency profiling and any kernel/quantization notes we should surface to the customer.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Model fit & evals follow-up — tool calling & structured output (Finlytics)

Folks — thanks, I'll run the pilot today and share the raw results + a short recommendation. Summary of the technical plan: 

1) Models to benchmark (pilot):
   - redwood-v2-large (float) — expected best quality baseline
   - redwood-v2-medium-quant (int8/quant) — cost/latency optimized; may trade some schema strictness
   - open-llama-7b-q4 — open baseline for cost comparison

2) Eval harness:
   - We'll run the 20-example prompt set through our function-calling harness (500 synthetic variations via gentle temperature/noise + arg permutations) to stress common failure modes.
   - Each run records: schema_pass (bool via JSON Schema validator), action_name (string), action_args (raw JSON), tokens, latency_ms.
   - We'll run three retry policies: no-retry, 1 retry, 2 retries. Retries will re-send the same request with an idempotency token; we'll detect duplicates via action_id and compare duplicate-action rates.

3) Success criteria (customer-facing):
   - Schema pass rate >= 95% on original prompt set (target).
   - Duplicate-action rate < 1% under 1-retry policy.
   - p95 latency <= 300ms on redwood-v2-medium-quant (if not achievable, we'll flag tradeoffs).

4) Implementation notes for Finlytics integration:
   - For retries, recommend including an idempotency_token field (UUID) in the function call metadata. Redwood SDK will forward that token to the ingest layer so replays are detectable.
   - Use deterministic decoding (top-k + low temperature or greedy) for action selection to reduce non-deterministic schema failures.
   - Apply a small post-process step: run a lightweight schema validator client-side and only accept final actions that pass; otherwise surface to the queue (we'll measure how often this happens).

Attached: finlytics_model_eval_prompt_set_v1.json (20 examples + synthetic generator config), finlytics_schema_spec_v2.json (as provided by Finlytics), redwood_benchmarks_tool_calling_q2_2027.pdf (internal benchmarks reference).

Next steps:
- I'll upload raw CSV of results to the Drive folder and send a short one-page recommendation by EOD.
- Marissa: can you schedule a 30-min review with Finlytics for Thursday? I'll bring recommended model + fallback and the tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
